original.title: Intrinsic Motivation and Self-Determination in Human Behavior

core_idea: People have three basic psychological needs: autonomy, competence and relatedness. When environments support these needs, people are more intrinsically motivated, internalize goals more fully and do better. Motivation is not just 'more or less' but differs in quality, from controlled (pressure, rewards) to autonomous (interest, values).
key_concepts_note: Use the concepts already stored for this theory in the library (theories.concepts).
when_to_use: What supports or undermines students', employees' or patients' motivation?
How do teaching, management or parenting styles relate to autonomy, competence and relatedness?
Typical data: validated scales (need satisfaction, motivation types), experiments, interviews.
common_mistakes: Treating motivation as a single amount instead of distinguishing types (intrinsic, identified, introjected, external).
Equating autonomy with independence. Autonomy means acting with volition, which can include relying on others.
Assuming rewards always undermine intrinsic motivation; effects depend on how rewards are given.
